judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Loss sustained by one Insured to the advantage of any other Insured' is compressed and its boundary — what counts as an advantage — is not stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Insured covers the parent, all subsidiaries and the plans (c074, c080), intercompany transfers could arguably fall inside it, straining Insuring Clause 1 (c048).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any person who is duly authorized by an Organization to have custody' is a very wide residual category tacked onto a list of institutional custodians.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That residual category duplicates the very custodians covered by the In Transit definition (c075) and Insuring Clause 3 (c050), so the exclusion threatens to swallow the grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any authorized representative of an Insured' is undefined and open-ended, and the trailing 'other fraudulent, dishonest or criminal act' is a catch-all after a list of named perils.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Authorized representative' is nowhere defined although Employee (c067), Executive (c069), Insurance Representative (c073) and Third Party (c089) are, leaving a gap the rest of the instrument does not close.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Or other similar representative' following agent, broker, factor, consignee and contractor is a textbook ejusdem generis catch-all, and the awareness triggers use undefined 'other fraudulent, dishonest or criminal act'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sub-paragraph (b) keys off awareness by an Executive or Insurance Representative, tying it to the Discovery definition (c066) and to Exclusion 12(n) (c103), which uses a different actor category.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two concrete limbs listing named perils and a mail/carrier exception; little play in the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It removes Forgery and Computer Fraud from Clauses 2 and 3 (c049, c050), which is the drafters' way of allocating perils among clauses; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Kidnap, ransom or other extortion payment (as distinct from Robbery)' asks the reader to police a line the policy does not otherwise draw.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parenthetical depends on the Robbery definition (c083) and the policy schedule refers to a separate Kidnap/Ransom coverage section not included in this Crime section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Registered or coupon obligation ... or any coupon whether attached or detached' is specific and technical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It narrows Insuring Clause 4 (c051) in a way that reinforces the paper-instrument reading of Financial Instrument (c070).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A sixty-day awareness cut-off keyed to an Organization becoming aware; 'becomes aware' is softer than the defined Discovery standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This exclusion is deleted in its entirety by Crime Endorsement No. 4 (c132), so the printed text no longer operates — a plain instrument-level inconsistency for a reader of the policy body.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excluding loss caused by 'any forgery or alteration of, on or in any written instrument' under a credit-card fraud clause is close to excluding the insured peril itself, and the lower-case 'forgery' differs from the defined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It nearly cancels Insuring Clause 8 (c055) and the Credit Card Fraud definition (c064) unless both provisos are satisfied, which is a genuine harmonisation problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three overlapping limbs (a), (b) and (c) about termination of the section, an Insuring Clause and the section 'in its entirety' say much the same thing in different words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This printed Exclusion 19 is replaced in its entirety twice over — by Endorsement No. 3 (c127), which drops the sixty-day notice window, and by Endorsement No. 5 (c134), which restores it with added words — leaving the operative text genuinely uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Owned by ... or for which the Organization is legally liable, or held ... in any capacity whether or not the Organization is liable' is broad but the three limbs are stated in the alternative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with Insuring Clause 9 and the Client definition (c056, c059) and with Exclusion 12(m) (c102), which limits custody-based coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Rewrites Insuring Clause 1 for plan losses and substitutes 'one (1) year' for 'sixty (60) days'; the substitution is mechanical and specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends Exclusion 19 by word substitution, but Endorsement No. 3 (c127) deletes the sixty-day language altogether while Endorsement No. 5 (c134) rewrites Exclusion 19 anew, so this substitution may have nothing left to operate on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two parallel limbs with prior-consent and reasonableness requirements; the drafting is careful.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its (a) limb depends on Insuring Clause 4 and Financial Instrument (c051, c070), and it is the express carve-out from Exclusion 12(i) (c098); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed acquisition mechanics with a ten-percent revenue test and a sixty-day notice deadline; 'sole discretion' is broad but expressly conferred.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its first paragraph is replaced by Endorsement No. 3 (c128), which changes coverage from 'after the effective date of such acquisition' to loss 'Discovered after' that date, so the printed text is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four cumulative conditions plus a non-stacking rule; long but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 3 (c129) deletes this Subsection 24 in its entirety, yet Subsection 25 as printed (c116) still opens 'Subject to Subsection 24' and the General Terms prior-policy clause (c036) covers overlapping ground.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The per-clause limit paragraphs are formulaic and repetitive but internally consistent; 'concerned or implicated' is the only elastic phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its first paragraph is replaced by Endorsement No. 3 (c130) with a discovery-based trigger, and its opening cross-reference to Subsection 24 refers to a subsection that endorsement deleted (c129).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two clear non-accumulation rules stated in absolute terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforces Subsection 25 (c116) and the prior-loss limit in c115, which the deleting endorsement (c129) has removed, leaving the anti-stacking scheme partly orphaned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At the earliest practicable moment' alongside hard ninety-day and six-month deadlines, plus a garbled (a)/(b) suit-limitation layout, gives a court something to sort out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Calling notice a condition precedent conflicts with the General Terms late-notice forgiveness (c021) and with Endorsement/Rider No. 1's prejudice requirement (c039-c041).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Least-of formulas keyed to published prices and specific dates; precise valuation mechanics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The General Terms valuation clause (c022) yields expressly to coverage-section provisions, so the two coexist; 'Lost Instrument Bond' is used but nowhere defined.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A four-step waterfall with a clear ordering and a reinsurance carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits with the General Terms subrogation clause (c023) and the Other Insurance clause (c121) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Declaring the section 'null and void to the extent of the amount recoverable' where other insurance exists is a strong formulation whose interaction with the proviso needs care.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion 12(m)(ii) (c102) contains a similar excess mechanism for other insurance, and the two excess clauses overlap on the same facts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-word amendment adding 'trustee' to the list of Executives; entirely mechanical and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supersedes subparagraph (a) of the printed Executive definition (c069), which remains in the policy body unamended on its face.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate about headings and unchanged terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other endorsement touches the Executive definition, so 'all other terms unchanged' operates cleanly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare deletion instruction; nothing to construe in the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It removes Exclusion 12(b) (c091) but the replacement privacy exclusions (c125) are considerably broader, so the net effect of the deletion is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Each limb ends 'including, but not limited to ... or any similar type of nonpublic information', an unbounded catch-all after a specific list, and 'loss involving' is far looser than 'loss resulting from'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The proviso preserves only Insuring Clause 6, leaving open whether a computer-fraud loss under Insuring Clause 5 (c052) that 'involves' spoofed identity information is excluded — a direct tension with that grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard headings and unchanged-terms boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'all other terms unchanged' formula is unremarkable here because no other endorsement addresses privacy exclusions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three limbs restate one idea in slightly different words, and as reproduced the lead-in carries stray '(1) (2)' markers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It rewrites Exclusion 19 'in its entirety' with no post-termination notice window, while Endorsement No. 5 (c134) also rewrites Exclusion 19 in its entirety and restores the sixty-day window — a head-on conflict between two same-dated endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Replaces the coverage trigger for acquisitions with a discovery-based one; the substituted text is short and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supersedes the first paragraph of Subsection 23 (c114) while the remainder of that subsection, with its sixty-day notice and premium conditions, survives unchanged.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any and all references to Subsection 24 are deleted in their entirety' is broad but plainly directed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It removes the prior-loss coverage in c115 while the General Terms prior-bond clause (c036) and the opening words of Subsection 25 (c116) still assume that architecture.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single substituted sentence combining a sustained-before-termination requirement with a discovered-during-the-period requirement; compact and clear on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires discovery during the Policy Period, whereas Exclusion 19 as amended by Endorsement No. 5 (c134) contemplates discovery and notice within sixty days after termination — the two cannot both be given full effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate headings and unchanged-terms language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'All other terms remain unchanged' is precisely what makes the clash between this endorsement's Exclusion 19 (c127) and Endorsement No. 5's Exclusion 19 (c134) unresolvable by ordering.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line deletion of a numbered exclusion; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deletes Exclusion 17 (c108), which nonetheless still appears in the policy body, so the operative text can only be determined by reading the endorsements together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing endorsement addresses Exclusion 17, so the unchanged-terms formula operates without friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reinstates the three-limbed sixty-day formulation and adds 'issued by the Company or by any affiliate of the Company' to the renewal proviso; the limbs remain redundant with one another.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends Exclusion 19 'in its entirety' in direct contradiction of Endorsement No. 3 (c127), which had already replaced Exclusion 19 with a no-notice-window version, and it also pulls against the amended Subsection 25 (c130).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate headings and unchanged-terms text, with a page-break artefact in the middle.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'all other terms unchanged' sentence is doing contested work given that Endorsement No. 3 (c127) had already rewritten the same Exclusion 19.
